attributes.founded: 17 December 1987, by Law 87/020, by merging the Department of Radio Broadcasting and Cameroon Television (CTV).
attributes.owner: The government of Cameroon, a public industrial and commercial establishment.
attributes.television: CRTV (the main channel), CRTV News (28 January 2018) and CRTV Sports and Entertainment (6 June 2019).
attributes.radio: The national station Poste National, regional stations and local FM services.
attributes.history: Began as Cameroon Television and later merged with the radio service.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Mass media in Cameroon and Telecommunications in Cameroon (CC BY-SA 4.0). Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: Law on social communication of December 1990

attributes.effect: Authorised the opening of private media. In practice private radio and television licences came much later and only partly.
attributes.licences: In August 2007 the government issued licences to two private TV broadcasters and one private radio broadcaster.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Mass media in Cameroon (CC BY-SA 4.0), and a Canal 2 International profile. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: Described as Cameroon's first private television channel.
attributes.launch: Launched in 2001 and renamed in 2004, according to one source. Wikipedia dates Canal 2 and STV to 2004.
attributes.reach: Received in the southern half of Cameroon and available by satellite and cable elsewhere.
attributes.owner_note: An older article says the only Cameroonian cable distributor, TV+, is owned by Emmanuel Chatue, who also runs Canal 2 International.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Media of Cameroon and Mass media in Cameroon (CC BY-SA 4.0). Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.names: Canal 2 International, STV (Spectrum TV), Equinoxe TV, Vision 4, Ariane TV, LTM TV, New TV, SAMBA TV, Liberty TV, KCBS Television and others.
attributes.closed: TV Max, the best known channel that broadcast illegally before liberalisation, closed in the early 2000s after a legal dispute with CRTV.
attributes.content: Many channels broadcast foreign programmes, including telenovelas, Hollywood and French films, mostly in French.
attributes.caution: Lists differ by year. Check current sources.
